profile.reading: This is the second of two nearly identical OpenStreetMap building footprints at 7300 World Communications Drive in Omaha, Nebraska, sitting roughly 65 to 75 meters from its companion record. Like its neighbor, this building was originally tagged MCI in 2019 and relabeled Verizon with a telecom=data_center tag in the same October 2023 changeset, a change that the edit history shows was based on aerial-imagery review rather than any documented site inspection or filing. MCI Communications, later MCI Inc, was a major long-distance and data-networking carrier that Verizon Communications acquired in January 2006, and much of MCI former network real estate, including switching centers and transport facilities, was absorbed into Verizon Business, the company enterprise and wholesale network arm. The presence of two similarly sized buildings at one address is consistent with a multi-building network campus, the kind of layout carriers use for switching equipment, transport gear, and backup power rather than colocation floor space sold to outside tenants. As with the companion building, no operator fact sheet, SEC filing, county assessor record, or trade-press piece naming this address as a Verizon or MCI site was found this session, so the specific current function of this building cannot be confirmed beyond the OSM tag itself. Nebraska sits outside the nine northeastern states plus the District of Columbia where Verizon operates as the legacy incumbent local exchange carrier through its Bell Atlantic and NYNEX heritage, which weighs against this being an old regional Bell central office and points instead toward MCI-inherited long-haul network infrastructure now under Verizon Business ownership, though that remains an inference rather than a documented fact. No capacity, square footage, tier rating, or construction year is claimed here because no source verifies those figures for this building.

reading.body:
The data cannot determine whether this Omaha facility currently supports AI workloads, as no power capacity is recorded and Verizon does not publish details on this site's customer base or use cases.

Two Verizon entries in this registry share the same address in Omaha, located roughly 90 meters apart on a street named for the facility itself. Research flags them as likely the same campus or adjacent buildings rather than separate locations. This suggests the registry still contains duplicates in areas where operators do not maintain public facility directories, and where commercial real estate listings alone cannot resolve the question.

Verizon's internal network switching and data facilities operate differently from the colocation sites that publish customer lists. Without published specifications or customer data, it remains unclear what traffic this location handles or whether it processes AI inference, training, or neither. The address is confirmed and the facility is real. What it does is not recorded here.
